To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we isolated and characterized a dog mastocytosis chymotryptase and found that it was related to other chymases and cathepsin-G.

the chymotryptase of dog mastocytic tumors is a serine proteinase with an Mr of 30,000, a high catalytic efficiency, and a unique octapeptide sequence that is conserved in other chymotrypsin-like proteinases of leukocytes.

we have isolated and characterized a serine proteinase (a chymase) from dog mastocymas that is related to the chymases from mast cells and cytotoxic T- and NK-cells of other species and to cathepsin-G, and that the chymases of all species sequenced to date share a common eight-residue sequence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation, purification and characterization of a chymotrypsin-like serine proteinase, chymase, from dog mastocytic tumours.
the purification and characterization of a chymotrypsin-like serine proteinase isolated from a mastocytoma.
the purification and characterization of dog chymase and its relation to other chymotrypsin-like serine proteinases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mastocytoma proteinase is a chymotrypsin-like serine proteinase which is a member of the chymotryptic serine proteinase family of leukocyte cells.
chymases from mast cells are serine proteinases that are closely related to cathepsin-G-type proteinases of granulocytes and cytotoxic T- lymphocytes.
the mastocytomas chymotrypsin-like proteinase is a chymase, and that it is a new member of the chymase subfamily of the proteinases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

chymase and tryptase are the major proteinase constituents of mast cells, that chymase is a chymotrypsin-like serine proteinase with a unique amino acid sequence, and that chymases from mast cells, neutrophils and cytotoxic T- and natural-killer cells share a common evolutionary origin.
dog mastocytomata chymase is closely related to the chymases of other species.

mastocytoma-derived chymase is a chymotrypsin-like serine proteinase that is related in sequence and enzymic properties to the chymotryptases of rat and human mast cell and to the chymases of cytotoxic T- and natural killer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the chymases from mastocytoma, rat peritoneal mast cells, rat small intestinal mucosal mast cells and human mast cells are closely related and that they are all members of a family of chymotryptically active serine proteinases that are found in leukocytes.
chymase is an enzyme that is present in a wide variety of leukocytes.
chymases are a distinct class of serine proteinases, with a common octapeptide sequence, that are expressed in a variety of leukocyte populations.
